label: EdgeRouter 12
description: EdgeRouter 12 (ER-12) - 10x 1G RJ45 + 2x 1G SFP. Powered by a 24V adapter, or by 24V passive PoE on eth0 (port 0) up to 20 W; eth9 (port 9) is an optional DC/PoE passthrough outlet, off by default.
notes: Quick Start Guide, https://dl.ui.com/qsg/ER-12/ER-12_EN.html : "Port 0 supports 24V Passive PoE In and port 9 supports optional Passive PoE Out (disabled by default)"; the Interfaces table reads "Port 0 Supports PoE IN; Port 9 Supports PoE Out", and the PoE table gives "PoE In: (1) 24V Passive PoE Port, 2-pair (4, 5+; 7, 8-)", "Passive PoE Max. Wattage Per Port 20W (24V, 0.83A)", "Max. Power Consumption 20W (Excludes PoE Output)". The tech-spec page (https://techspecs.ui.com/uisp/wired/er-12) prints the same 20 W per-port ceiling under "Passive PoE Voltage range Max. wattage per port: DC/PoE passthrough 20W (24V)" and the same 20 W device draw. So eth0 is the one inlet and declares the router's own ceiling, 20 W, which is also the stated per-port maximum; the other nine copper sockets declare poeIn: false. Before this, the device-wide poe-pd capability put 12.95 W on all ten sockets - 129.5 W of demand on a 20 W router. eth9's PoE Out is not modelled as a PSE here: Ubiquiti prints "DC/PoE Passthrough" with no budget of its own (the output is the input supply), so a per-port budget would have to be invented; see the ER-X row for how that table is recorded when the vendor prints the input-source rows.
